--- title: "Estimation, Confidence Intervals & Bootstrap" description: "Move beyond point estimates with uncertainty intervals and bootstrap simulation that works far beyond simple means." author: "MLStation" date: 2026-10-01 categories: [Statistics, Inference, Bootstrap, Data Science] draft: false --- A point estimate answers: > What is my best single-number estimate? An interval asks the more honest question: > **How uncertain is that estimate?** ::: {.callout-tip} ## What you will learn - Point estimators, bias and variability - Confidence intervals - Bootstrap resampling - Coverage as a repeated-sampling property - How bootstrap uncertainty applies to ML metrics ::: ## Estimate + uncertainty For a mean under a normal approximation, $$ \bar x \pm z_{1-\alpha/2}SE(\bar x) $$ gives a familiar confidence interval. But the interpretation is often misstated. A 95% confidence procedure is designed so that, over repeated samples, about 95% of intervals produced by the procedure cover the fixed true parameter. ## Animation: watch 95% intervals succeed and fail ```{ojs} //| echo: false viewof repsCI = Inputs.range([10,200], {value:50, step:5, label:"Repeated samples"}) rci=d3.randomLcg(.55) rowsCI=d3.range(repsCI).map(i=>{ let vals=d3.range(25).map(()=>d3.randomNormal.source(rci)(0,1)()); let m=d3.mean(vals), se=d3.deviation(vals)/5, lo=m-1.96*se, hi=m+1.96*se; return {i,m,lo,hi,cover:lo<=0&&hi>=0} }) coverage=d3.mean(rowsCI,d=>d.cover) html`
Observed coverage${(100*coverage).toFixed(1)}%
` ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false Plot.plot({ height:420,x:{label:"Estimate / interval"},y:{label:"Repeated sample"}, marks:[ Plot.ruleX([0],{strokeDasharray:"4,4"}), Plot.ruleY(rowsCI,{y:"i",x1:"lo",x2:"hi",stroke:d=>d.cover?"#4F46E5":"#E11D48"}), Plot.dot(rowsCI,{x:"m",y:"i",fill:d=>d.cover?"#4F46E5":"#E11D48",r:3}) ] }) ``` ## Bootstrap: let the sample imitate repeated sampling Given observed data: ```text Original sample ↓ sample WITH replacement Bootstrap sample 1 → statistic Bootstrap sample 2 → statistic ... Bootstrap sample B → statistic ↓ Approximate sampling distribution ``` ::: {#0663c1eb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} import numpy as np import plotly.express as px rng=np.random.default_rng(11) x=rng.lognormal(mean=1,sigma=.8,size=80) B=5000 boot=np.array([np.median(rng.choice(x,size=len(x),replace=True)) for _ in range(B)]) lo,hi=np.quantile(boot,[.025,.975]) print("Median:",np.median(x),"Bootstrap 95% interval:",(lo,hi)) fig=px.histogram(x=boot,nbins=60,labels={"x":"Bootstrap median"}) fig.add_vline(x=lo,line_dash="dash"); fig.add_vline(x=hi,line_dash="dash") fig.update_layout(height=360) fig.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Median: 2.7963995533835746 Bootstrap 95% interval: (np.float64(2.3574487124359127), np.float64(3.832847807494673)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## DS/ML Bridge: uncertainty for model metrics Bootstrap can estimate uncertainty for: ```text accuracy AUC RMSE precision / recall business lift feature summaries ``` provided the resampling scheme respects the data structure. Time series, clustered observations and repeated users require more care than i.i.d. rows. ::: {.callout-warning} ## Bootstrap is not magic Resampling a biased or unrepresentative dataset does not make it representative. The bootstrap approximates variability around the empirical sample you actually collected. ::: ## Summary - Point estimates need uncertainty. - Confidence level describes a repeated-sampling procedure. - Bootstrap approximates a sampling distribution by resampling observed data. - Bootstrap is especially useful for complicated statistics and ML metrics. - Resampling must respect the structure of the data. **Next:** *Hypothesis Tests, p-values, Errors & Power*
